explanation.text:
A composed and uniform trust in God and a constant course of integrity are urged in view of the blessedness of the truly pious, contrasted in various aspects with the final ruin of the wicked. Thus the wisdom and justice of God's providence are vindicated, and its seeming inequalities, which excite the cavils of the wicked and the distrust of the pious, are explained. David's personal history abundantly illustrates the Psalm. (Psa. 37:1-40)

The general sentiment of the whole Psalm is expressed. The righteous need not be vexed by the prosperity of the wicked; for it is transient, and their destiny undesirable.

bsb.title: Of David.
bsb.text: Do not fret over those who do evil; do not envy those who do wrong.

explanation.text: For they shall soon be cut down like the grass, and wither as the green herb. Which in the morning looks green, pretty, and flourishing, and in the evening is cut down, and then fades away; see Psalm 90:5; and so the wicked prosper and flourish for a while, and then they perish with all their honour, riches, and wealth; so that their happiness is a very short lived one, and therefore need not be envied and fretted at.

bsb.text: For they wither quickly like grass and wilt like tender plants.

explanation.text:
Trust--sure of safety.

shalt thou dwell--or, "dwell thou"; repose quietly.

verily . . . fed--or, "feed on truth," God's promise (Psa 36:5; compare Hos 12:1).

bsb.text: Trust in the LORD and do good; dwell in the land and cultivate faithfulness.

explanation.text: desires-- (Psa 20:5; Psa 21:2), what is lawful and right, really good (Psa 84:11).

bsb.text: Delight yourself in the LORD, and He will give you the desires of your heart.

explanation.text:
Commit thy way-- (Pro 16:3). Works--what you have to do and cannot set forth as a burden.

trust . . . in him--literally, "on Him." He will do what you cannot (compare Psa 22:8; Psa 31:6). He will not suffer your character to remain under suspicion.

bsb.text: Commit your way to the LORD; trust in Him, and He will do it.

explanation.text:
And he shall bring forth thy righteousness as the light,.... That is, the good man having committed his cause to him that judgeth righteously, he will, in his own time, clearly make it appear that it is a righteous one, both to himself and others, in whatsoever obscurity it may have lain;

and thy judgment as the noonday; the same as before, unless rather the righteousness of Christ, which is the believer's by imputation, and is a justifying one in the judgment of God, should be meant; see Micah 7:9; and the phrases may denote not barely the revelation of it in the Gospel, but the more clear manifestation of it to the believer himself, from faith to faith; or as it will be still more clearly revealed and declared at the day of judgment, when those who are clothed with it shall shine as the sun in the kingdom of their Father, and be clear of all those charges and imputations which they have lain under in this life.

bsb.text: He will bring forth your righteousness like the dawn, your justice like the noonday sun.

explanation.text:
Rest in--literally, "Be silent to the Lord."

and wait--Be submissive--avoid petulance and murmurings, anger and rash doing.

bsb.text: Be still before the LORD and wait patiently for Him; do not fret when men prosper in their ways, when they carry out wicked schemes.
Refrain from anger and abandon wrath; do not fret—it can only bring harm.

explanation.text: Two reasons: The prosperity of the wicked is short; and the pious, by humble trust, will secure all covenant blessing, denoted here by "inherit the earth" (compare Psa 25:13).

bsb.text: For the evildoers will be cut off, but those who hope in the LORD will inherit the land.

explanation.text: shall not be--literally, "is not"--is not to be found.

bsb.text: Yet a little while, and the wicked will be no more; though you look for them, they will not be found.

explanation.text: peace--includes prosperity.

bsb.text: But the meek will inherit the land and delight in abundant prosperity.

explanation.text: gnasheth . . . teeth--in beastly rage.

bsb.text: The wicked scheme against the righteous and gnash their teeth at them,

explanation.text:
(Compare Psa 2:4).

seeth--knows certainly.

his day--of punishment, long delayed, shall yet come (Heb 10:37).

bsb.text: but the Lord laughs, seeing that their day is coming.

explanation.text:
sword, and . . . bow--for any instruments of violence.

slay--literally, "slaughter" (Sa1 25:11).

poor and needy--God's people (Psa 10:17; Psa 12:5). The punishment of the wicked as drawn on themselves--often mentioned (compare Psa 7:15-16; Psa 35:8).

bsb.text: The wicked have drawn the sword and bent the bow to bring down the poor and needy, to slay those whose ways are upright.

explanation.text:
Their sword shall enter into their own heart,.... As Saul's did into his, 1 Samuel 31:4;

and their bows shall be broken; the meaning is, that their efforts shall be fruitless, and their attempts in vain; the mischief they have contrived and designed for others shall fall upon themselves; see Psalm 7:15; and therefore the saints should not be fretful and envious.

bsb.text: But their swords will pierce their own hearts, and their bows will be broken.

explanation.text: riches--literally, "noise and tumult," as incidental to much wealth (compare Psa 39:6). Thus the contrast with the "little" of one man is more vivid.

bsb.text: Better is the little of the righteous than the abundance of many who are wicked.

explanation.text: Even the members of the body needed to hold weapons are destroyed.

bsb.text: For the arms of the wicked will be broken, but the LORD upholds the righteous.

explanation.text: God, who knows His people's changes, provides against evil and supplies all their need.

bsb.text: The LORD knows the days of the blameless, and their inheritance will last forever.

explanation.text:
They shall not be ashamed in the evil time,.... Of affliction and persecution, or of old age, or in the day of judgment, when it will go ill with others; see 1 John 2:28;

and in the days of famine they shall be satisfied: whether it is understood figuratively of a famine of hearing the word, or literally of a proper famine of bread and water: these God will provide for them, as he did for Elijah, and they shall be sure unto them, and therefore let them not fret nor envy.

bsb.text: In the time of evil they will not be ashamed, and in the days of famine they will be satisfied.

explanation.text: While the wicked, however mighty, are destroyed, and that utterly, as smoke which vanishes and leaves no trace.

bsb.text: But the wicked and enemies of the LORD will perish like the glory of the fields. They will vanish; like smoke they will fade away.

explanation.text: payeth not--not able; having grown poor (compare Deu 15:7). Ability of the one and inability of the other do not exclude moral dispositions. God's blessing or cursing makes the difference.

bsb.text: The wicked borrow and do not repay, but the righteous are gracious and giving.

explanation.text: cut off--opposed to "inherit the earth" (compare Lev 7:20-21).

bsb.text: Surely those He blesses will inherit the land, but the cursed will be destroyed.

explanation.text: steps--way, or, "course of life"; as ordered by God, failures will not be permanent.

bsb.text: The steps of a man are ordered by the LORD who takes delight in his journey.
Though he falls, he will not be overwhelmed, for the LORD is holding his hand.
I once was young and now am old, yet never have I seen the righteous abandoned or their children begging for bread.

explanation.text: his seed is blessed--literally, "for a blessing" (Gen 12:2; Psa 21:6). This position is still true as the rule of God's economy (Ti1 4:8; Ti1 6:6).

bsb.text: They are ever generous and quick to lend, and their children are a blessing.

explanation.text: The exhortation is sustained by the assurance of God's essential rectitude in that providential government which provides perpetual blessings for the good, and perpetual misery for the wicked.

bsb.text: Turn away from evil and do good, so that you will abide forever.
For the LORD loves justice and will not forsake His saints. They are preserved forever, but the offspring of the wicked will be cut off.

explanation.text:
The righteous shall inherit the land,.... See Gill on Psalm 37:9 and See Gill on Psalm 37:11;

and dwell therein for ever; See Gill on Psalm 37:27.

bsb.text: The righteous will inherit the land and dwell in it forever.

explanation.text: The righteous described as to the elements of character, thought, word, and action.

bsb.text: The mouth of the righteous man utters wisdom, and his tongue speaks justice.

explanation.text: steps--or, "goings"--for conduct which is unwavering (Psa 18:36).

bsb.text: The law of his God is in his heart; his steps do not falter.

explanation.text: The devices of the wicked against the good fail because God acquits them.

bsb.text: Though the wicked lie in wait for the righteous, and seek to slay them,

explanation.text:
The Lord will not leave him in his hand,.... Or power; but will in his own time deliver him from all the reproach, affliction, and persecution endures by him; as he will also deliver him out of all the temptations of Satan;

nor condemn him when he is judged; by the wicked man: he will not join in the sentence, but reverse it, and condemn the tongue that rises up in judgment against him, and save him from him; see Psalm 109:31; nor will the Lord condemn him when he is judged by him at the hast judgment; but will acquit him before men and angels, and introduce him into his kingdom and glory.

bsb.text: the LORD will not leave them in their power or let them be condemned under judgment.

explanation.text: On the contrary, the good are not only blessed, but made to see the ruin of their foes.

bsb.text: Wait for the LORD and keep His way, and He will raise you up to inherit the land. When the wicked are cut off, you will see it.

explanation.text: of which a picture is given, under the figure of a flourishing tree (compare Margin), which soon withers.

bsb.text: I have seen a wicked, ruthless man flourishing like a well-rooted native tree,

explanation.text: he was not--(Compare Psa 37:10).

bsb.text: yet he passed away and was no more; though I searched, he could not be found.

explanation.text: By "the end" is meant reward (Pro 23:18; Pro 24:14), or expectation of success, as in Psa 37:38, which describes the end of the wicked in contrast, and that is cut off (compare Psa 73:17).

bsb.text: Consider the blameless and observe the upright, for posterity awaits the man of peace.

explanation.text: together--at once; entirely (Psa 4:8).

bsb.text: But the transgressors will all be destroyed; the future of the wicked will be cut off.

explanation.text:
strength-- (Psa 27:1; Psa 28:8).

trouble--straits (Psa 9:9; Psa 10:1). In trust and quietness is the salvation of the pious from all foes and all their devices.

Next: Psalms Chapter 38

bsb.text: The salvation of the righteous is from the LORD; He is their stronghold in time of trouble.
The LORD helps and delivers them; He rescues and saves them from the wicked, because they take refuge in Him.
